description: Canonical TSV schema + entity-resolution layer — turns heterogeneous RawRecords from any adapter into coherent, deduplicated, Neo4j-import-compatible node and edge TSV files keyed on a stable global id reconciled to Wikidata QIDs and Getty ids, with typed headers, provenance, and round-trip-safe canonical ordering.

userStories.title: Implement the canonical TSV header model
userStories.description: As a developer, I need typed node/edge headers matching docs/data-model.md so files are Neo4j-import compatible.
acceptanceCriteria: Define NodeSchema and EdgeSchema describing required headers (csid:ID, :LABEL, name, ...) and typed property suffixes (:int, :float)
Provide a function to render and parse a header row for nodes and for edges
Reject property columns whose declared type suffix does not match the data model
Tests pass (pytest) round-tripping a header row to schema objects and back
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Implement a strict TSV writer and reader
userStories.description: As a developer, I need tab-delimited IO that never corrupts data containing tabs/newlines so files are lossless.
acceptanceCriteria: Writer escapes/encodes tab, newline, and backslash in field values deterministically; reader reverses it exactly
Multi-value fields use ';' with a defined escape for literal ';'
Header is always the first line; column order is stable
Tests pass (pytest) writing then reading values containing tabs, newlines, and ';' and asserting equality
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Implement csid minting
userStories.description: As a developer, I need deterministic global ids so re-runs are idempotent.
acceptanceCriteria: If a Wikidata QID is known, csid is derived deterministically from it (e.g. cs:<type>:Q<number>)
Otherwise csid is cs:<type>:<deterministic slug/hash of normalized name+lang>
Minting the same input twice yields the identical csid
Tests pass (pytest) covering QID-based and name-based minting determinism
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Implement field normalization
userStories.description: As a developer, I want raw fields cleaned into canonical columns so downstream matching is reliable.
acceptanceCriteria: Normalize whitespace, unicode (NFC), and trim; map common source field names to canonical column names via a configurable mapping
Parse temporal values into time_start:int / time_end:int (BCE negative) and keep raw in time_start_iso when ambiguous
Parse coordinates into lat:float / lon:float; invalid coords are dropped with a logged warning
Tests pass (pytest) for date parsing (BCE, century, year ranges) and coordinate parsing
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Map RawRecords to canonical node rows
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a RawRecord-to-node-row mapper so any adapter's output reaches the canonical schema.
acceptanceCriteria: Produce a node row with csid, :LABEL from the category spec, name, lang, and any resolved dimension columns
Carry provenance columns (source, source_url, source_query, retrieved_at, confidence) onto every row
Unknown/extra raw fields are preserved in a dedicated overflow column rather than dropped
Tests pass (pytest) mapping a fixture RawRecord set to node rows
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Implement Wikidata QID reconciliation
userStories.description: As a developer, I want entities matched to Wikidata so the same thing from two sources gets one id.
acceptanceCriteria: When a row lacks a QID, attempt reconciliation via the Wikidata search/reconciliation API (cached client) using name+type+lang
Accept a match only above a configurable score threshold; otherwise leave QID null and lower confidence
Record the reconciliation decision (matched/none/ambiguous) in provenance
Tests pass (pytest) against a recorded reconciliation API fixture covering match, no-match, and ambiguous cases
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Implement Getty id reconciliation against local dumps
userStories.description: As a developer, I want entities anchored to AAT/TGN/ULAN where applicable so vocabularies normalize types/places/people.
acceptanceCriteria: Build an in-memory index from the local Getty dumps (from acquisition Tasklist) keyed by normalized preferred label
Attach getty_id to a node when a confident label+type match exists
No false anchor: ambiguous matches are skipped and logged
Tests pass (pytest) against a small Getty index fixture
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Implement deduplication / entity resolution
userStories.description: As a developer, I want duplicate entities collapsed so the graph has one node per real-world thing.
acceptanceCriteria: Resolution precedence: identical wikidata_qid > identical getty_id > exact normalized (name,lang,type) > fuzzy name match above threshold
Merging unions aliases, keeps the highest-confidence value per column, and concatenates provenance from all merged rows
Merge decisions are recorded so they can be audited and reversed
Tests pass (pytest) merging a fixture with QID-dupes, label-dupes, and a fuzzy near-duplicate
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Generate MEMBER_OF_CATEGORY and INSTANCE_OF edges
userStories.description: As a developer, I want each entity linked to its scraped category and type so categories are queryable.
acceptanceCriteria: For every node, emit a MEMBER_OF_CATEGORY edge to the category node and an INSTANCE_OF edge to its type node
Category and type nodes are created (idempotently) if absent
Edges carry provenance from the source rows
Tests pass (pytest) asserting edge counts equal node counts for a fixture category
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Implement canonical sorting for round-trip stability
userStories.description: As a developer, I want deterministic file ordering so TSV diffs are meaningful and Neo4j round-trips are stable.
acceptanceCriteria: Node files sorted by csid; edge files sorted by (:START_ID, :END_ID, :TYPE)
Column order follows the schema's canonical order exactly
Writing the same logical dataset twice yields byte-identical files
Tests pass (pytest) asserting byte-stability across two writes
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Implement a schema/data validator
userStories.description: As a user, I want to validate TSV files so malformed data is caught before import or export.
acceptanceCriteria: Validate: required headers present, typed columns parse, csid unique, edges reference existing csids, provenance non-empty
Report errors with file, line, and column context; exit non-zero on failure
Validator runs on both node and edge files in a directory
Tests pass (pytest) on a valid fixture (passes) and several invalid fixtures (each fails with the right message)
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Add a normalize CLI command
userStories.description: As a user, I want one command that turns raw .jsonl from acquisition into validated canonical TSV.
acceptanceCriteria: Add `culturescrape normalize <raw.jsonl> --category <category.yml> --out <dir>` producing nodes/<type>.tsv and edges/<type>.tsv
Pipeline runs: map -> normalize -> reconcile -> dedup -> edges -> sort -> validate
Running on a fixture raw file produces valid TSV that passes US-011 validation
Tests pass (pytest) invoking the CLI end-to-end on a fixture
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Document the schema and reconciliation behavior
userStories.description: As a user, I want clear docs so I can trust and extend the normalization layer.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/schema.md documents every canonical column, type suffix, escaping rules, and the resolution precedence
Include a worked example: two raw rows for the same dish from Wikidata + wikitext merging into one node
All code examples in the doc run as a doctest or referenced test
Tests pass (pytest) for the worked-example test
Lint passes (ruff)
